page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server belonging to the n4 family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs, which correspond to 4 physical Intel cores utilizing hyper-threading with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 16 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include any local storage or GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The underlying Intel processor is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8) for accelerated matrix operations. Cryptographic acceleration is provided via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI flags. In benchmark testing, the CPU achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1672.09 and a multi-core score of 7217.53, while the Geekbench multi-core score reached 7215.0.

Memory performance benchmarks show a read-only large block bandwidth of 68.85 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 40.33 GB/sec, though the overall Passmark memory score is relatively weak at 1718.22. For database and web workloads, the server handles 8.82 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers a static web serving throughput of 11.89 GB/sec. Large language model inference speeds on a medium 7B model reach 52.37 tokens/sec for prompt processing, but drop to a weak 7.92 tokens/sec during text generation.

Given its low memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-bound tasks that do not demand large memory footprints. The hardware profile is suited for workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, lightweight vector calculations, and parallelized integer processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server featuring 8 dedicated Intel vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, this instance relies on its Intel processor, which includes AVX-512 and AMX extensions, backed by a 260 MB L3 cache. Performance benchmarks place it in the average tier, with a Passmark CPU score of 12045.57 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 7215.0. While memory performance is relatively weak, with a Passmark memory score of 1718.22, it handles Redis SET operations at 8.82 million operations per second and static web serving at 11.89 GB/sec. This configuration is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy, memory-light workloads such as software compilation, web serving, and basic vector processing.
